searchText: as per this (pseudo sql-ish) query https://dune.com/queries/3383110/5677040 30/80 have more than 100k ETH staked considering both entry and exit queues we should be at 20%-ish with supernodes would be very valuable Where does the 20% figure come from? That seems quite high. based on standard vcs attached to the bn number by institutions But yes, I think these big staking entities will split their huge stake into many 2048 ETH validators, ideally spread across many nodes. It would cool to reach out & ask them what their expected setups will look like post-Pectra. we can ask lido/ethstaker for these mean numbers than counting registrations > It would cool to reach out & ask them what their expected setups will look like post-Pectra. exactly That would a lot easier lol then take a considerable error margin/ tolerance value and test with that % Not ethstaker though. They aren't a staking entity. let's say if they say 6 vcs to 1 bn, we can try a supernode % that would back calculate to 9 vcs, which would result to even lesser supernodes than a real-ish mainnet situation oops, coinbase it is then they are top 2, lido, coinbase I heard that at least some liquid staking protocols are not going to consolidate fast because their entire infra (rewards calculation etc.) is optimised for 32 ETH stakes. It may take years for them to update the infra and eventually consolidate. More centralized entities should not have this problem. Hey y'all, curious what kurtosis file are you guys using currently? I tried to use the one defined in https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/peerdas-devnet-4#Kurtosis-Interop-Conifg-Pre-devnet-testing, but prysm seems to panic with `ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:peerDAS-01705d1` image 🙏 cc: <@531934490826768418>
